# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 30 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 30 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_030_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 3, continued — On Falsehood in Business

**1** "Now I command you to love truthfulness. Guard truthfulness, that it may always remain with you. **2** Beloved, let only that be in your mouth which is worthy of God, and let no falsehood whatsoever enter it. **3** You were commanded to love truthfulness. Love it therefore and keep it." **4** I said to him, "Sir, sometimes in our business dealings and in our other transactions we speak falsely — not because we want to sin but because we are forced to. Can we be saved?" **5** He said to me: "You will be saved if you do not do it willfully. For those who speak a false word willfully, those are the ones who sin. But those who are forced and speak falsely, even though it is involuntary, they do not greatly sin; and if they repent it will be forgiven them. **6** But the one who speaks falsely voluntarily, that person harms himself, for that is his way of life — he has chosen it. You therefore, be on your guard concerning this commandment, and keep it, that you may not bring yourself into trouble."

---

*EMET note: Ch. 30 is a practical extension of Mandate 3 — addressing involuntary/compelled falsehood in business. The Shepherd introduces a distinction between deliberate lying and compelled falsehood, with different moral weights. This is sophisticated moral casuistry.*
